title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Online-Based Intervention “Novego: Out of Burnout” – A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of the 6-week online program “Novego: Out of Burnout”, a digital web-based support intervention designed to reduce symptoms in individuals diagnosed with burnout (ICD-10: Z73.0). 

A total of 246 participants will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group (IG) or a wait control group (WCG). All participants will complete self-report questionnaires at four time points: before the intervention, immediately after program completion, and three and six months later. 

It is expected that participants in the intervention group will show greater improvements in symptoms, overall health status, and quality of life compared to the control group, with effects remaining stable throughout the follow-up period.

interventions.name: Intervention group = access to the 6-week internet-based support program „Novego: Out of Burnout“
Waitlist control group = receives no additional treatment during the intervention period (only ‘care as usual’); receives access to the intervention after 6 months (after the last follow-up)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
One of the following diagnoses according to ICD-10 (confirmed by a medical specialist or psychotherapist): Z73.0 

Internet access to use the intervention 

Sufficient knowledge of the German language 

PSS-10 total score ≥ 22 points at baseline 

Informed consent and willingness to participate in the study, including four anonymous online assessments via the online survey tool Qualtrics and independent use of the intervention 

Valid email-address 

Patients should have a stable therapeutic situation (pharmacotherapy and/or psychotherapy or waiting period) for at least four weeks prior to randomization and should maintain this as consistently as possible throughout the study period
Exclusion criteria:
Lifetime diagnosis of a psychotic or bipolar disorder 

Acute suicidal behavior within the past four weeks 

Dementia disorders 

Current use of high-potency and/or atypical antipsychotics 

Presence of a serious illness that, in the opinion of the principal investigator, excludes participation of the patient in the study until its completion
